description: A question is a specific kind of post; question records form a subset of the post records discriminated by the post type.
An answer is a specific kind of post; answer records form a subset of the post records discriminated by the post type.
A user account is composed of the posts it owns; every post carries an author reference to the owning account, and the author reference is absent only where the account record no longer exists.

connection_condition: answer posts reference their parent question through posts.ParentId
description: A question is composed of the answers given to it; an answer cannot exist without the question it responds to.
A post is composed of the comments attached to it; a comment has no meaning detached from its post.
A user account is composed of the comments it authored; the author reference is present for almost every comment, and it is the authoritative link to the commenting account.
A post is composed of the votes cast on it; every vote targets exactly one post.

connection_condition: votes.UserId corresponds to users.Id, populated only for a small minority of vote records
description: A user account is composed of the votes it cast. Unlike authorship, voter attribution is mostly absent: only a small fraction of vote records identify the voter.
A user account is composed of the badges awarded to it; each badge award belongs to one recipient.

connection_condition: postLinks.PostId and postLinks.RelatedPostId both reference posts.Id
description: A post is composed of the link records in which it participates, either as the source post or as the related post.

connection_condition: the tag tokens embedded in the delimited tag list of a question denote the same tags as tags.TagName, but the two are written in different surface forms
description: The tags carried by a question and the tag catalogue entries express the same business concept of a topic label. The embedded tag list uses a delimited token form while the catalogue stores a bare name, so the same tag is represented differently in the two places.

A display name is the human-readable label by which a person is named in questions; it is an attribute of a user account rather than a stable identifier, and several accounts may share the same label.
The calendar year is derived from the year component of a creation timestamp and is used to bucket records annually.
The calendar year for user activity is derived from the year component of the last-access timestamp.
The average view count is derived as the mean of the individual view counters across the qualifying question posts.
The average user age is derived as the mean of the individual age values across the qualifying users, considering only users whose age is recorded.
The post-to-vote ratio is derived by dividing the number of posts attributed to a user by the number of votes attributed to that same user; both terms in the quotient must share one user scope.
The badge year share is derived by counting awards of one badge kind within a year and dividing by the total count for that badge, so that two years become comparable as percentages.
Post score and comment score share the same name but measure votes on different entities and live in different tables; they must not be treated as interchangeable when a question says only 'score'.
